fields.sample_size: Vhembe District Municipality, Limpopo, South Africa: 12 experts (managers, technicians and engineers of the technical water services department) interviewed face to face, purposively sampled with a target of at least half of the identified experts; plus literature and policy review; interview dates not stated
fields.effect_measure: thematic narrative analysis of semi-structured interviews (no counts of respondents per theme); descriptive household figures from the Local Government Handbook
fields.effect_estimate: Participants described reliance on taps, boreholes, rivers, dams and weirs; because the district lags in piped provision, communities use untreated or contaminated sources (risk of diarrhoea and cholera), residents of Tswinga village collect water from neighbouring villages, and illegal connections follow poor service in Thulamela and Mutale. The district is understaffed and financially constrained (rural projects in Ntshabalala and Mulima delayed), its water service provision strategy needs periodic review and alignment with other sector plans, and the water supply reconciliation strategy developed with the Department of Water and Sanitation measures service levels by cluster. The authors conclude that South Africa has strong policies and frameworks but lacks capacity and political will to implement, and recommend aligning district and local municipal plans, involving civic organisations (SANCO), universities and community forums, and using the District Development Model. Context figures: Vhembe has 7.4% of households with piped water inside the dwelling and 16% with a flush toilet connected to a sewer.
fields.section: Full text (14 pages, MDPI Soc. Sci. 12:614): Methods (case study design, purposive sampling); Discussion and Findings 8.1-8.8; Conclusions and recommendations

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative case study of intergovernmental relations in water service provision in one South African district municipality (12 expert interviews); read in full text 2026-10-04. Narrative themes only; no effect estimate.
